content_html:
Free Energy Principle (FEP)

Organisms maintain their order by minimizing variational free energy — an upper bound on sensory surprise under a generative model. In brains, this appears as predictive coding: top-down predictions meet bottom-up evidence; differences (prediction errors) drive learning and action.

Perception–action loop (Active Inference)

Perception updates beliefs to fit data; action changes data to fit beliefs. Both reduce free energy. Precision (attention) controls the influence of prediction errors.

Equation (intuition)

F = Eq[ ln q(s) − ln p(s, o) ].

Free energy F is minimised when internal beliefs q(s) approximate the true posterior over hidden causes p(s|o) under a generative model p(s, o). This provides an upper bound on surprise, −ln p(o), which organisms cannot compute directly.

Hierarchy & timescales

Low levels (ms–s)

  • Edges, tones, proprioception
  • Fast error correction

Mid levels (s–min)

  • Objects, words, gestures
  • Perceptual categorisation

High levels (min–years)

  • Goals, identity, narratives
  • Policy selection; planning

Practice: three levers to lower free energy

  • Update beliefs (learning): increase model fidelity.
  • Act (sampling): move to confirm predictions or seek new evidence.
  • Tune precision (attention): weight errors appropriately to avoid over/under-fitting.
